fields.sample_size: documentary case study of the 2020-2021 private concession of sanitation services in Rio de Janeiro state (47 municipalities in four blocks): financial data from 86 official documents (pre-feasibility studies behind the auction notice), literature, and records of public debates (state legislature front against privatisations; forum Agua e Vida, nao Mercadoria) in 2020-2021; no interviews
fields.effect_measure: qualitative and documentary analysis with financial figures from the auction documents; no inferential statistics
fields.effect_estimate: The first auction on 30 April 2021 sold four blocks of municipalities (inside and outside the metropolitan region) for 35-year concessions; the fixed grant paid totalled R$ 22.7 billion, an agio of 121% over the minimum R$ 10.3 billion, with a 4.7 billion investment expected from one block; the concession is meant to bring 99% water and 90% sewage coverage by 2033 through R$ 31 billion of investment in 47 municipalities and up to R$ 1.8 billion for informal settlements and favelas. Revenue sharing: 80% of the fixed grant to the state, 15% to municipalities by population and 5% to the metropolitan fund; the agio is split 50-50 between state and municipalities, who also receive a variable 3% of tariff revenue (0.5% to the metropolitan fund). The authors argue that fiscal austerity and financialisation led planners to design a model that subordinates spatial regulation to profitability and captures public rents now while leaving the promised universalisation in the peripheries uncertain; the STF ruling in ADI 1842 on shared metropolitan ownership of sanitation is part of the setting.
fields.section: Full text (Portuguese, about 25 pages, Scripta Nova 29(3)): Introduction (method); financialisation and planning; the Rio de Janeiro concession (auction, grant, revenue sharing); Discussion; Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Introduction (documents and debates analysed); section on the auction results and revenue sharing; Scripta Nova 29(3)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a documentary case study of the Rio de Janeiro sanitation concession design (86 official documents plus public debates) with auction and revenue-sharing figures; read in full text 2026-10-04. No outcome measurement and no counterfactual.
